title: [DNS Client] Wrong IP when resolving many domain names (conflict)
body:
### Version

vert.x 3.9.1

### Context

I encountered an unexpected response from the DNS Client while requesting ip for 4 domain names. Every x seconds, I'm checking the IP for 4 domaine names...
Sometimes I got an error `DNS query timeout for xxx` and the IP for the domain `xxx` is affected to another domain `yyy`

This is due to `inProgressMap` and the random id.

DNS is using UDP, so the only way to know which answers corresponds to which query is by using id... So here we are caching queries in a map by their id.
https://github.com/eclipse-vertx/vert.x/blob/f451dcde8f7908a00466ffa6f1d4712ac0fb0ce3/src/main/java/io/vertx/core/dns/impl/DnsClientImpl.java#L49-L51

But with random ids, we can possibly find the same twice in a row... 
https://github.com/eclipse-vertx/vert.x/blob/f451dcde8f7908a00466ffa6f1d4712ac0fb0ce3/src/main/java/io/vertx/core/dns/impl/DnsClientImpl.java#L297-L305

And in this case, the previous query will be overridden :disappointed:.
https://github.com/eclipse-vertx/vert.x/blob/f451dcde8f7908a00466ffa6f1d4712ac0fb0ce3/src/main/java/io/vertx/core/dns/impl/DnsClientImpl.java#L340-L353

### Do you have a reproducer?

Yes, [MainVerticle.java](https://gist.github.com/Joxit/e96b036b81a27e7377763d1bdf307731)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start your onw DNS server (do not DDoS Official DNS servers...) I'm using consul
```sh
# Start consul as daemon with docker
docker run -e CONSUL_ALLOW_PRIVILEGED_PORTS=true -d --name consul --network host consul agent -dev -dns-port=53
# Register domain names for the reproducer
docker exec consul consul services register -name one -address 10.0.0.1
docker exec consul consul services register -name two -address 10.0.0.2
docker exec consul consul services register -name three -address 10.0.0.3
docker exec consul consul services register -name four -address 10.0.0.4
```
2. Start the MainVerticle
3. In general the issue appear between 1 and 5 minutes. You will see something like `Wrong ip due to id conflict, received 10.0.0.3 instead of 10.0.0.4`

### Extra

OS: Debian 10.5 Buster :rocket: 
Java: OpenJDK 14
Docker: 19.03.12 (for consul)

### Solutions

In the [DNS Specification](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2181) I found this:
```
4. Server Reply Source Address Selection

   Most, if not all, DNS clients, expect the address from which a reply
   is received to be the same address as that to which the query
   eliciting the reply was sent.  This is true for servers acting as
   clients for the purposes of recursive query resolution, as well as
   simple resolver clients.  The address, along with the identifier (ID)
   in the reply is used for disambiguating replies, and filtering
   spurious responses.  This may, or may not, have been intended when
   the DNS was designed, but is now a fact of life.
```

So the common usage is to use both the ID and address.

**First solution**:
Move `inProgressMap` from `<Integer, Query>` map to <String, Query> map. The string can be something like `${id}/${address}`

**Second solution**:
Move `inProgressMap` from `<Integer, Query>` map to <Pair<Integer, String>, Query> map. This one requires more code but may be easier to maintain ?

:warning: When your query looks like `one.service.consul` in the response (`DnsResponse`) it will be `one.service.consul.` with a final dot.
